sources.title: Policy attachment
sources.text: Policy version A: cancellation notice period is 48 hours.

sources.title: Website policy
sources.text: Policy version B: cancellation notice period is 24 hours. Effective date is not recorded.

sources.title: Booking
sources.text: Customer booked on 20 October 2026. Cancellation was received 30 hours before the scheduled visit. The accepted policy version is not recorded.

brief.summary: Sources show two policy versions (48-hour and 24-hour notice) and a booking with cancellation received 30 hours before the visit. Which policy the customer accepted and the effective date of version B are not recorded.

timeline.title: Booking made
timeline.detail: The booking record states the customer booked on 20 October 2026.

timeline.title: Cancellation received
timeline.detail: The booking record states the cancellation was received 30 hours before the scheduled visit. The exact timestamp and timezone are not given.

citations.quote: Cancellation was received 30 hours before the scheduled visit.

uncertainties: Which policy version (A or B) the customer accepted is not recorded.
The effective date of Policy version B is not recorded.
Exact timestamps and timezones for the cancellation and the scheduled visit are not given; only a 30-hour interval is stated.
The dates of the cancellation and the scheduled visit are not stated.
The sources do not state whether any payment was made or what any payment amount was.
questions: Which policy version was presented to or accepted by the customer at booking, and is there acceptance evidence?
When did Policy version B take effect relative to the 20 October 2026 booking?
What are the exact timestamps and timezones of the cancellation and the scheduled visit?
How was the 30-hour figure calculated, and from what record?

issues.title: Which cancellation policy version governs the booking
issues.why: Policy A sets a 48-hour notice period and Policy B sets 24 hours. A 30-hour interval is shorter than 48 hours but longer than 24 hours, so the policy version affects how the notice interval compares with the stated period. This brief does not decide which policy applied.
missing: Evidence of which policy version the customer accepted
Effective date of Policy version B
Date the Policy A attachment was provided, if at all

relations.quote: Policy version A: cancellation notice period is 48 hours.
Policy version B: cancellation notice period is 24 hours.
The accepted policy version is not recorded.

issues.title: Verification of the 30-hour cancellation interval
issues.why: The 30-hour figure is the only stated measure of notice. Without timestamps and timezones, the interval cannot be independently confirmed against either policy's notice period.
missing: Method used to calculate the 30 hours
